clue.text: Auditor's fixed prices for sculpture

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so what follows is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: a price freeze holds prices fixed

explanation.surface: An accountant reports on the set prices charged for works of sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but here it is simply a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorated band of carved relief along a wall is a classic form of architectural sculpture.

clue.text: Mad rebel retains a lawyer-that should be interesting

indicators.note: retains means keeps inside, so the jumbled letters hold the rest
mad means crazed, so the letters of rebel are jumbled

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A crazy rebel keeps a lawyer on, which should make for an interesting story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' scrambles the rebel and 'retains' wraps it round the rest; DA is the American District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that is engaging and pleasant to get through is described as worth reading.

clue.text: Urgent need for one to replace article in old bureau

indicators.note: to replace means the letter for one takes the place of the article

parts.note: ex means former or old
an agency is an office or bureau
a is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old office urgently needs one person to stand in for a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: In EXAGENCY, 'to replace' swaps the article A for I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing demand or emergency requirement is a formal synonym for an urgent need.

clue.text: German princess charged for cutting half her hair?

indicators.note: cutting half means only the front half of the word for charged is kept

parts.note: electrically charged things are electric
a tress is a lock of a woman's hair

explanation.surface: A German noblewoman is billed for having half her hair cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means billed in the surface; here it is ELECTRIC, cut in half to ELEC.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Holy Roman Empire the wife of a prince-elector held this title.

clue.text: My question's not about disguising impressive skill …

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: disguising changes how something looks, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not here asks for the word for about to be absent from the word before it

parts.note: the word question itself, with the 's as a link
on can mean about, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: Someone whose question avoids its topic hides an impressive talent, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sentence into the next clue; 'not about' removes 'on' (about), then 'disguising' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura of special, almost magical expertise surrounding a performer is their mystique.

clue.text: Easy profit from selling hemp?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for payment earned for little or no effort
taken literally, hemp is what ropes are made of, so selling it brings cash for cord

explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means gain for no effort; literally it is cash for used cord, which is made from hemp.

clue.text: With a gin, perhaps, relax chatting in a bar

parts.note: a gin is a snare for animals, an example of a trap

indicators.note: chatting means speaking, so what matters is how the word for relax is pronounced

parts.note: to ease is to relax

explanation.surface: Someone with a gin and tonic unwinds over conversation in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A gin is not the drink but an animal snare. 'chatting' signals that EASE is spoken, giving EZE.
explanation.definitionFit: The swinging horizontal bar used by circus acrobats is a bar of this kind.

clue.text: Start to hedge after half a dozen games

definitions.meaning: living cuttings, usually hawthorn, planted to grow into a hedge
a tennis set won six games to love is over fast

explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is just a link. The second reading is whimsical: six straight games make a speedy tennis set.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names slips of hawthorn set in the ground as the beginning of a hedgerow.

clue.text: Contrive to be a driver along American lines

definitions.meaning: to contrive is to bring about by planning or scheming
in the US the driver of a railway locomotive goes by this title

explanation.definitionFit: To contrive is to scheme something into being, and Americans call a train driver by this word.

clue.text: … of Italian astronomer — almost all I gather is peripheral

indicators.note: peripheral means lying on the outside, so the word for gather wraps around the rest

parts.note: to glean is to gather bit by bit

indicators.note: almost means the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a speaker claims most of what they collect about an Italian stargazer is marginal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of' the astronomer means belonging to him. 'almost' and 'is peripheral' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Galileo, the Italian who studied the heavens with a telescope.

clue.text: Sending a message by errand-boy, receiving nothing in return

indicators.note: receiving means the word for errand-boy takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a fag is a junior pupil who runs errands for a senior at a British public school

indicators.note: in return means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sends a note by a messenger boy and gets no reply.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is a junior boy who ran errands for seniors at old British boarding schools; 'in return' and 'receiving' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmitting a document over a telephone line by machine is a way of sending a message.

clue.text: Woolly fabrication? One needs hanging for that!

definitions.text: Woolly fabrication? One needs hanging for that!

parts.words: Woolly fabrication? One needs hanging for that!
parts.note: reads like a vague lie that deserves the gallows, but describes a woven woollen piece displayed on a wall

explanation.surface: A muddled lie is so bad its teller deserves the noose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabrication' means a made thing, not a lie, and 'hanging' is wall display, not execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven wall hangings of wool are made pieces of fabric meant to be hung up.

clue.text: A fool in a jacket

parts.note: a jerk is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot wearing a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting sleeveless leather coat of old is a type of short jacket.

clue.text: Brave' woman's infiltrating drug scene, finally

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the woman's word goes into the drug

parts.note: coke is slang for cocaine
her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word scene

explanation.surface: A courageous woman goes undercover in the drugs world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American warrior is called a brave, and this nation of the south-east US is one tribe.

clue.text: Ignore as irrelevant murder in cold blood

definitions.meaning: to discard or rule out from consideration
to kill deliberately, as a gangster disposes of a rival

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both ruling something out of consideration and killing someone coolly and deliberately.

clue.text: Quails, possibly, in the company of women

definitions.meaning: the collective noun for a group of quails
a group of girls or women, as in a party of ladies

explanation.definitionFit: The same collective word names both a flock of game birds and a gathering of young women.

clue.text: Partly covered in Webster — new revised edition

indicators.note: revised means edited and altered, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A new revised edition of Webster's dictionary is partly covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges WEBSTER plus N; 'edition' just carries the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scattered over a surface, like petals on a path, leaves it partly covered.

clue.text: See adult liable to get soaked in a mist

parts.note: v is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references
A is the film classification for adult
something porous lets water in and gets soaked

explanation.surface: A grown-up likely to get drenched in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: V for vide (see) is a reference-book convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full of vapour or fog-like haze, the adjective describes something in a mist.

clue.text: You'll see this in a twinkling

definitions.text: You'll see this in a twinkling

parts.words: You'll see this in a twinkling
parts.note: in a twinkling sounds like an instant, but a point of light in the night sky literally twinkles

explanation.definitionFit: Celestial lights shimmer as their light passes through the atmosphere, the familiar twinkle of the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: One used to slip into a brogue

definitions.text: One used to slip into a brogue

parts.words: One used to slip into a brogue
parts.note: brogue suggests an Irish accent, but it is a sturdy shoe, and the tool eases a foot into it

explanation.definitionFit: A curved tool of horn or metal helps the heel slide into a tight shoe such as a brogue.

clue.text: A sign tank's miles away

indicators.note: away means the abbreviation for miles goes missing from the tank word

parts.note: a fish tank is an aquarium, plus the 's

explanation.surface: A notice says the tank is a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes M (miles) from AQUARIUM'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The water carrier is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Villa-like construction seen to cause amazement

parts.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, so Villa suggests Aston
the suffix ish means like or somewhat

explanation.surface: A building in the style of a villa is seen to stun onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club; 'construction' only says the answer is assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound or stun someone is to cause them great amazement.

clue.text: Collected a bulk edition

parts.note: mass means bulk or size

explanation.surface: Someone gathered a large printing of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering or accumulating things in quantity is what heaping them together means.

clue.text: Sort of quadruped — a hard worker

definitions.meaning: the wooden horse of Troy, a four-legged figure
someone who works like a native of Troy toils tirelessly

explanation.walkthrough: To 'work like a Trojan' is a British idiom for working very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse of Troy is one kind of horse, and the idiom makes a Troy native a tireless toiler.

clue.text: Private road giving awkward view when inside vehicle

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the word for vehicle

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ungainly, so the letters of view are put out of order

explanation.surface: A private lane gives a poor outlook from inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' suggests a car, but it is a brewer's cart; 'awkward' and 'inside' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A short private access road leading from the street to a house is called this.

clue.text: I set out to secure work — I must look after myself

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the scrambled letters enclose the word for work
out means put out of order, so the letters of I set are scrambled

parts.note: go can mean work or function, as in the engine won't go

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to get a job, telling themselves they must take care of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I SET into EIST, which 'to secure' wraps round GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person whose motto is taking care of number one is an egotist of this kind.

clue.text: Most of the stars can encompass a peak in this composition

indicators.note: encompass means surround, so the trimmed constellation goes round the rest
most of means the last letter of the constellation is dropped

parts.note: Orion is a well-known constellation, a group of stars
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Most celebrities are capable of reaching a high point in this musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hill in south-west England; 'Most of' and 'encompass' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-scale sacred musical work for voices and orchestra, like Handel's Messiah, is a composition.

clue.text: I do seven cryptic clues, plunging in

definitions.note: a noun phrase here, a steep plunge or dive

indicators.note: cryptic clues mix letters up, so the words I do seven are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver dives straight into seven puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep headlong downward plunge, as by an aircraft, is a dive of this kind.

clue.text: Queen given cosy accommodation in Worthing?

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: The monarch is put up in a snug place in a Sussex seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Worthing is a Sussex resort, but here it is the surname of the hero of Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Oscar Wilde's comedy, Jack Worthing goes by this first name in town.
